alerts_tx.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 16 at 6:54AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
alerts_tx.area: Guadalupe; Caldwell; Fayette; Wilson; Karnes; Gonzales; De Witt; Lavaca
alerts_tx.description:
Fog has developed with lighter winds across a corridor from near
New Braunfels/San Marcos eastward through Gonzalez into La Grange.
Visibility is currently trending of around 1 mile or less with
patchy dense fog at times to around 1/4 of a mile. Expect for the
visibility to improve within a hour or two of sunrise. Drivers
use caution by slowing down, allowing extra room between your
vehicle and the vehicle in front of you, and keep on the low beam
headlights.

alerts_tx.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 16 at 1:13AM CDT until August 16 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
alerts_tx.area: Blaine; Caddo; Jackson; Tillman; Comanche; Cotton; Wilbarger; Wichita; Archer; Clay
alerts_tx.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 108.

* WHERE...In Oklahoma, Blaine, Caddo, Comanche, Cotton, Jackson, and
Tillman Counties. In Texas, Archer, Clay, Wichita, and Wilbarger
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
alerts_tx.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

alerts_tx.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 15 at 11:49PM CDT until August 16 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
alerts_tx.area: Montague; Cooke; Grayson; Fannin; Lamar; Young; Jack; Wise; Denton; Collin; Hunt; Delta; Hopkins; Stephens; Palo Pinto; Parker; Tarrant; Dallas; Rockwall; Kaufman; Van Zandt; Rains; Eastland; Erath; Hood; Somervell; Johnson; Ellis; Henderson; Navarro; Anderson
alerts_tx.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 107 and temperatures up to 105.

* WHERE...Most of North Texas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
alerts_tx.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

alerts_tx.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 15 at 10:06PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts_tx.area: Inland Kenedy; Southern Hidalgo; Inland Willacy; Inland Cameron
alerts_tx.description:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce
heat index values between 108 and 111 degrees for several hours
Sunday afternoon and evening. A few locations may briefly
experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

If spending time outside on Sunday, drink plenty of water, wear
light weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.
